title: Massaman Beef Curry
description: Hybrid method. Optional cast iron sear, then a long gentle braise in the bowl. Should read sweet and gently sour rather than hot.

source.name: Cross-checked against Thai and Thermomix sources

confidence.note: Cross-checked against Thai and Thermomix sources.

items.note: Or 1 brown onion cut into petals

items.item: jasmine rice, coriander and extra crushed peanuts

steps.text: Toast the spices. Cinnamon stick ({{cinnamon}}), cardamom ({{cardamom}} pods), star anise ({{star-anise}}) and cloves ({{cloves}}) into the dry bowl. Dry fry 5 min / 100°C / Speed 1, MC off. Tip out and wipe the bowl.

Sear the beef (optional). Pat the beef ({{beef}}) very dry and sear hard in the cast iron in batches, about 2 minutes a side. Do not crowd it. Skip this for the more traditional route; the paste and long braise carry the dish without it.
Shallots ({{shallots}}) into the bowl. Chop 3 sec / Speed 5. Scrape down.

Crack the paste. Add the curry paste ({{paste}}) and 2 tbsp of the thick cream from the top of the tin. Sauté 4 min / 120°C / Speed 1 until fragrant and the oil visibly separates. This is the step that makes the dish.

Braise. Add the beef, the remaining coconut cream ({{coconut}} total), fish sauce ({{fish-sauce}}), tamarind ({{tamarind}}), palm sugar ({{palm-sugar}}), the toasted spices and bay leaves ({{bay}}). Cook 90 min / 100°C / Reverse / Soft stir, MC off with the simmering basket on the lid to vent steam.

Add the vegetables. Potatoes ({{potatoes}}), carrot ({{carrot}}) and peanuts ({{peanuts}}). Cook 20 min / 100°C / Reverse / Soft stir, same lid setup. If the beef is still firm, extend before this step rather than after, or the potatoes collapse.
Rest 10 minutes off heat, uncovered. Season now: fish sauce for salt, tamarind or lime for sourness, palm sugar for depth.
Serve over jasmine rice with coriander and crushed peanuts.

notes.title: No salt until the end
notes.text: The paste and fish sauce are both high sodium. Taste at step 7 and adjust then.

notes.title: Capacity
notes.text: These amounts land near 1.9L, under the 2.2L line but not by much. Do not scale up.

notes.title: Cut
notes.text: Chuck or gravy beef only. Leaner cuts go dry over this braise time.

notes.title: Cardamom substitute
notes.text: ¼–½ tsp ground stands in for 4 pods, added with the paste at step 4 rather than the start of the braise. A pinch each of cinnamon and clove also works.

notes.title: Raw peanuts
notes.text: Blanched raw peanuts in the braise are fine and have traditional precedent, they just soften. Roast a handful separately for the garnish to get the crunch back.
